name: Isolated MCP installation and client configuration
summary: Installs a bundled MCP runtime in extension storage, gates publication on dependency audit and health checks, and updates only the selected project's VibeKnowledge MCP configuration entry.
limitations: Reviewed setup orchestration, configuration editing, audit policy, build wiring and selected tests, not the full MCP server/tool/RAG implementation or external registry state.

The build references packages/mcp-server/scripts/health-check.mjs, but that file was absent in this isolated source copy. Its actual protocol/native-SQLite assertions and end-to-end bundle completeness could not be verified.
Tests were inspected, not run. No dependencies were installed, no audit/network request or native runtime handshake was executed, and no user MCP configuration was changed.

facts.text: knowledge.setupMcp and the Knowledge settings menu are registered before workspace/database initialization. Installation requires workspace trust, uses a configured absolute target or a local-folder chooser, confirms project/configuration paths modally, and reports cancellable progress through an output channel. Concurrent invocations only show that channel while selection/installation is active.

Machine-scoped knowledgeGraph.mcp settings select workspacePath, external nodePath, optional absolute npm-cli.js, client and audit timeout. Auto client detection checks vscode.env.appName for Cursor. The resolved external Node must be >=26.1.0 <27 (no prerelease); npm must be 11+. Setup uses that Node's execPath and prepends its directory to subprocess PATH.

The UI passes extension/dist/mcp-server as bundle and globalStorageUri/mcp as storage to setupMcp. esbuild's asset phase builds portable Node-26 ESM server files, copies runtime metadata/lock/config and shared graph modules, plus audit and health-check helpers. The server package declares MCP SDK ^1.22.0 and better-sqlite3 ^13.0.3; these are external runtime dependencies, unlike the extension's sql.js database initializer.

setupMcp resolves the target directory and validates its existing JSONC before running downloads. Each attempt gets a unique staging directory under extension storage, with an identity derived from lock bytes and Node/platform/architecture. It copies the bundle and runs npm ci --omit=dev --audit --ignore-scripts there, never in the business project.

A separate production audit gates setup: only a complete valid report with zero high/critical findings and successful process status counts as clean. Unavailable service, malformed output and timeouts are not success. The validated per-request timeout is 10–120 seconds (default 60); retryable failures get at most three attempts with 2/4-second backoff, under a larger enclosing process limit.

After audit, the UI-provided ensureDatabase creates graph.sqlite only if missing, via DatabaseService.initialize/close. setupMcp then invokes health-check.mjs with the workspace and a 45-second timeout before configuration publication. Setup does not generate graphs, and the generated server arguments disable RAG; users still must trust/start or restart the server in their MCP client.

jsonc-parser (root dependency ^3.3.1) edits only servers.vibeknowledge for .vscode/mcp.json or mcpServers.vibeknowledge for .cursor/mcp.json. VS Code adds type: stdio; both use the resolved Node, staged dist/index.js, --workspace and --rag-mode none. Parsing allows comments/trailing commas, rejects malformed roots/server maps, and preserves surrounding fields/comments with JSONC edits.

Immediately before publication, setup compares mcp.json to its initial text and refuses detected concurrent edits. A nonempty prior config gets a timestamped .bak; replacement uses a unique temporary file and rename. Failed attempts remove only their staging directory; successful/older installs remain so existing processes keep working. Preserved MCP config does not imply zero side effects: the chosen workspace setting is saved earlier and a missing database may already have been initialized.

Process execution uses spawn with argument arrays, shell:false and windowsHide:true. AbortSignal/timeouts terminate the child tree (taskkill on Windows, process-group signals elsewhere); output is bounded and common credential forms are redacted. UI cancellation/disposal aborts the active controller, and errors direct users to setup logs/settings.

MCP setup tests assert JSONC preservation/client shapes, Node bounds, isolated process arguments/order, backups, timeout propagation, stage-failure cleanup, concurrent-edit refusal and cancellation. Most orchestration uses an injected mocked process runner; separate tests exercise real argument passing/process cancellation. Command tests assert early registration, workspace trust blocking and audit-timeout forwarding; bundle tests assert expected helper/assets and no shipped node_modules/src.
